title: SIEM customer contract and connector checklist
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a lightweight customer-facing contract + internal checklist for SIEM export integrations (Splunk HEC, Datadog logs, Azure Sentinel/Event Hub). It captures customer requirements we need to sign off on, the connector feature contract (schema + delivery guarantees), RBAC and audit implications, and an acceptance test checklist for pre-prod handoff.

Quick note: this is a working draft — expect TODOs and open questions. The aim is to have a single-page contract a sales/CS lead can hand a customer during onboarding, plus a dev checklist for the connector engineer.

1) High-level customer contract (one-paragraph summary to include in onboarding emails)
- Redwood will deliver a continuous export of production audit and activity logs related to the customer tenancy to the customer’s designated SIEM endpoint(s). Exports follow the "Connector Field Contract v1" schema (field set + schema_version header) and include the following event classes: auth events, admin activity, inference requests (metadata only), model rollouts and deploys, RBAC changes, and evidence generation events. Delivery modes supported: Splunk HEC (HTTPS with token), Datadog Logs (HTTP/S or TCP with API key), Azure Event Hub/Log Analytics (SAS or Managed Identity).

2) Required customer inputs (what CS asks the customer before we start)
- Primary SIEM type: Splunk / Datadog / Sentinel
- Endpoint details: HEC URL or Datadog intake URL or Event Hub namespace + hub name
- Auth mechanism: token (HEC/Datadog) or SAS + AAD/MI for Azure
- TLS requirements: TLS1.2+ enforcement, client cert if required
- Retention requirements: min retention (days), PII retention exemptions
- Allowed IP ranges for push (if customer restricts ingestion)
- Field mapping expectations: whether customer expects our canonical schema or a custom field map (we prefer canonical)
- Throughput expectations (events/sec, peak burst) and SLO for ingest latency (e.g., <= 30s for low-latency monitors)
- Contact points and on-call window for connector troubleshooting

3) Connector Field Contract v1 (canonical fields we will always send)
- schema_version: string (e.g., "v1.0") // top-level header in each payload
- event_id: string (uuid)
- timestamp: iso8601 string UTC
- tenant_id: string (redwood tenancy id)
- product_area: string (e.g., "hosted-api" | "dedicated" | "private")
- event_type: string (auth | admin | inference_request | model_deploy | rbac_change | evidence_generated | system_alert)
- actor: string (email or service principal)
- actor_role: string (RBAC v2 role at time of event)
- resource: string (resource id or name)
- resource_type: string (route | model | deployment | organization | project)
- outcome: string (success | failure | partial)
- details: string (freeform short description)
- metadata: JSON-string (optional freeform map for connector-specific fields)

Notes:
- For Splunk HEC we will send JSON events in the standard HEC format with the above as the "event" object plus fields.hec_index when provided.
- For Datadog we will map event_type to "ddsource" and include all canonical fields as attributes.
- For Sentinel via Event Hub we will wrap events as newline-delimited JSON with schema_version and tenant_id in each record.

4) Required vs optional fields and PII guidance
- Required fields: schema_version, event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, event_type, actor (anonymize on request), outcome.
- Optional: metadata, resource_type, actor_role (if RBAC v2 not yet enabled for a tenant we will send "unknown").
- PII: actor by default is human-readable email; if the customer requests PII minimization we will hash the actor (sha256) and provide a mapping artifact under strict contract (stored in Redwood vault and shared via secure transfer). Must be agreed in contract addendum.

5) RBAC v2 mapping considerations
- Redwood's RBAC v2 introduces role scoping by project and route. For SIEM consumers we emit actor_role as the effective role at the time of the event, plus metadata.role_scope = "project:<id>" if applicable.
- When customers request mapping to their internal role names, we must agree on a mapping table; do not attempt to translate without explicit mapping. Add mapping to "linked_artifacts" in onboarding ticket.

6) Delivery guarantees and latency SLOs (what Redwood commits to)
- Best-effort, at-least-once delivery for HEC/Datadog Event APIs. We'll include sequence ids and retry metadata in the event for idempotency reconciliation.
- For Event Hubs (Sentinel) use checkpointing on our side; duplicates can occur.
- SLO targets (negotiable): 99% of events delivered within 30s; 99.9% delivered within 5m for standard export. For strong SLAs (Dedicated/Private) we can tighten with reserved bandwidth.

7) Acceptance tests (Dev -> CS handoff checklist)
- [ ] Schema conformance: run connector against sample events and validate against JSON schema (unit tests exist in repo).
- [ ] End-to-end flow: send 1k synthetic events across 10 event_types and confirm arrival in SIEM index/hub.
- [ ] Latency test: measure median and p95 end-to-end latency for a 1-minute 50rps burst.
- [ ] RBAC labels: create RBAC v2 changes and confirm actor_role and role_scope present in resulting events.
- [ ] PII mode: confirm actor is hashed when PII minimization is requested.
- [ ] Failure modes: simulate SIEM auth failure and confirm connector backoff and alerting triggers.
- [ ] Backpressure and rate-limiting: verify connector respects customer-specified max QPS and graceful drop strategy documented in incident playbook.

8) Customer-facing onboarding steps (to include in the email template)
- Step 1: Customer provides endpoint details + auth token/SAS + allowed IPs
- Step 2: Redwood provisions connector config and shares a pre-prod test token
- Step 3: Customer runs a short ingest test (we provide curl examples) and shares logs/acknowledgements
- Step 4: Redwood runs 10-minute load test and shares raw results + sample events
- Step 5: Customer signs acceptance or opens issues (we have 5 business days SLA to resolve pre-prod issues)

9) Sample curl / payload snippets (quick samples for CS)
- Splunk HEC: curl -k -H 'Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"event":{ "schema_version":"v1.0","event_id":"...","timestamp":"2026-02-15T12:00:00Z","tenant_id":"t-123","event_type":"inference_request","actor":"svc:frontend","outcome":"success","metadata":"{"tokens":34}"}}' https://siem-customer:8088/services/collector/event

- Datadog: POST to https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input/<APIKEY> with JSON body being the canonical event. Include ddsource instead of event_type if requested by customer.

- Sentinel/Event Hub: send newline-delimited JSON to Event Hub namespace; ensure schema_version and tenant_id per line.

10) Troubleshooting notes (quick internal runbook bullets)
- If events not arriving: check network (IP allowlist), token validity, TLS handshake errors. Most common fail: customer IP restriction and wrong HEC port.
- If duplicate events observed: confirm connector is emitting at-least-once; advise dedupe by event_id on SIEM side.
- If fields missing: check schema_version mismatch; connector releases may add fields only in newer schema_version. Ask CS to confirm schema agreed.
- If latency > SLO: measure queue backlog on connector host; check for GC pauses, CPU contention, or downstream throttling from SIEM.

11) Operational and security controls (short)
- Secrets: tokens stored in KMS and rotated every 90 days by default. Customer can request shorter rotation windows.
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ enforced. For on-prem/private deployments customer can supply client certs; we will support mutual TLS where required.
- Audit trail: every config change to connector will produce an internal audit log event (rbac_change) that is included in exports. This satisfies evidence automation requirements for many auditors.

12) Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want to include raw request payloads for inference_request events in production exports? (privacy/cost tradeoff). TODO: propose opt-in flag for payload_trim_level: none | metadata_only | full_truncated.
- Should we support Syslog (UDP) for legacy SIEMs? Current priority is HEC/HTTP-based endpoints. TODO: product review.
- Add standardized sample dashboards and saved-searches per SIEM (Splunk SPL, Datadog query, KQL) — owner: Marco.

13) Acceptance sign-off (place to capture customer signoff in ticket)
- Customer name: __
- SIEM type: __
- Endpoint provided: __
- Agreed schema version: v1.0
- PII mode: default | minimized | hashed
- CS rep: __
- Date: __

Appendix: quick KQL / SPL examples (one-liners)
- Splunk (find failed auths): index="redwood_customer" event_type=auth outcome=failure | stats count by actor
- Datadog (failed model deploy events): @event_type: "model_deploy" AND @outcome:"failure" | count()
- Sentinel (KQL for admin changes): RedwoodLogs | where event_type == "rbac_change" | summarize count() by actor, tostring(metadata.role_scope)

End of draft.

Notes-to-self: attach the JSON Schema file from repo before final; check with legal about hashed actor mapping addendum. Follow up with Solutions Engineering for prebuilt dashboards and add to playbook.
